tools.name: find_skills
tools.description: Up to three skills from the aiqbench library that fit a task, each with a trust score, one line on what it adds for this task (why), the context cost in tokens, a URL to read the skill (use once) and an install command; a skill judged not to help is left out. The task text is matched and not stored

tools.name: get_skill
tools.description: The SKILL.md and file list of one skill, to follow for the current task without installing it. What you read is exactly what aiqbench scanned. To read a skill find_skills suggested, pass its id: several skills share a name, and a name returns the best-trusted of them. Otherwise name it as the user w

tools.name: install_command
tools.description: The one-line install command for a skill in a given agent, where it lands, and its page on aiqbench.

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "find_skills" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Up to three skills from the aiqbench library that fit a task, each with a trust score, one line on what it adds for this task (why), the context cost in tokens,…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: find_skills · Private data: find_skills, get_skill · Public sink: find_skills, get_skill.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: find_skills · Private data: find_skills, get_skill · Public sink: find_skills, get_skill

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
